scenes.say: Wait—what's the real difference between a Docker image and a container? This one sticks if you get the picture.
scenes.img: A giant cargo ship at a busy port, with stacks of identical sealed shipping containers waiting to be loaded. Dock workers point at a blueprint, then at the containers.

scenes.prompt: A dock worker holds up a detailed blueprint (image) next to a physical shipping container (container) being loaded onto the ship. The blueprint is crisp and clean; the container is scuffed and has stickers from travel.
scenes.say: Think of an image as the blueprint, and a container as the actual box shipped out. One blueprint, many boxes.
scenes.img: A dock worker holds a crisp blueprint next to a scuffed shipping container being loaded onto a ship. Stickers and dents show the container's unique journey.

scenes.label: Image
scenes.sub: A read-only template, built in layers.
scenes.say: An image is read-only. It's built in layers, like stacking blueprints for each step.
scenes.img: Dock workers stacking transparent blueprints on a table, each layer adding details to the final design.

scenes.label: Container
scenes.sub: A running copy with its own changes.
scenes.say: A container is a running copy. It gets its own writable layer—stickers, dents, whatever happens on the trip.
scenes.img: A shipping container with new stickers and dents being rolled onto the ship, dock workers waving it off.

rows.b: Write on the box, not the plan

scenes.say: Build an image, run as many containers as you want. Each can scribble on its own box, but the blueprint stays clean.
scenes.img: Dock workers assembling boxes from blueprints, each box getting unique marks as it's loaded onto the ship.

scenes.question: Is an image a running app?
scenes.right: Nope! It's just the template. The container is the running app.
scenes.say: Interview trap: Is an image a running app? Nope! It's just the template. The container is the running app.
scenes.img: A confused dock worker tries to drive a blueprint, while another drives an actual container onto the ship.
A proud dock worker gives a thumbs-up in front of a ship loaded with containers, blueprints tucked under their arm.
